name: modal

open.note: [element] visibility; reflects to el.open. el.show()/el.hide() also work.

title.note: header title (default variant) AND the bold heading in the confirm variant (variant="confirm").

icon.note: [element] confirm-variant icon (a library key, e.g. timesCircle)

confirm-variant.note: the footer confirm button variant — any obs-button variant; primary (default) or error (destructive) are the common ones.

scrollable.note: [element] fixed-height body with its own scroll

summary: Centered dialog over a dimmed backdrop. MModal (39x) is the base; FlotoConfirmModal (71x) is the confirm variant. Open via trigger slot or open prop. No x/backdrop-close (footer/Escape only).

behaviors.open: trigger slot (open fn) or open prop
behaviors.close: header x / footer Cancel / Escape (verified) / success — NO built-in x, NO backdrop-close (closable/maskClosable hardcoded false)
behaviors.confirm: Cancel(default) left, action right; error variant for destructive

headerPattern: built-in x is off, so real modals (~26) add their own header in the title slot: flex row with a text-primary title + a close x (MIcon times wired to hide())

overlayVariants.scrollable-modal: fixed-height scrollable body, top 50px, rounded header; modifiers restrict-width (1020px), smaller-modal (50vh)

accessibility.semantics: role=dialog; Ant traps + restores focus; Escape closes (even with x hidden)
accessibility.gaps: F1 no visible close besides footer; SF-001 no focus ring inside

decisionFlow: A yes/no or DESTRUCTIVE confirmation? -> obs-modal variant="confirm" (confirm-variant="error" for destructive).
A focused short task/form that must INTERRUPT the flow? -> obs-modal (the default dialog).
Long/complex content, or a panel CONTEXTUAL to a record (details/edit in place)? -> obs-drawer (side panel), NOT a modal.
A full-screen flow / wizard? -> a page or obs-drawer, NOT a modal.
Just a brief transient message? -> a notification/toast, not a modal.

dialog(MModal).useWhen: a focused task/form that interrupts the flow; short content
dialog(MModal).must: include a footer Cancel (only visible way out — F1)

confirm(FlotoConfirmModal).useWhen: confirm a yes/no or destructive action
confirm(FlotoConfirmModal).example: Delete monitor? (error variant, Cancel/Delete); delete in CRUD lists, inline-name-edit, trap-profile

hide-footer.useWhen: view-only content (no Save/Cancel); header x is the way out

scrollable-modal.useWhen: long body that must scroll (lists/editors); wrap content in flex:1;min-height:0;overflow-y:auto (F3)
scrollable-modal.example: Compare metric, linked-records detail, widget JSON editor, column configurator

no-padding.example: log-collection profile list, view-query, LAMA integration, activation-code modal

drawer-instead.useWhen: content is long or contextual to a record -> use FlotoDrawer (158x), not a modal

MModal.useWhen: A focused, self-contained task or short form must interrupt the flow until the user finishes or dismisses it. Open via the trigger slot ({ open }); build your own header (title + close x) and a footer ({ cancel, success }); size with width/centered, use confirmLoading for async Save.
MModal.dontUse: Don't use for yes/no or destructive confirmations (use FlotoConfirmModal), and don't use for long or record-contextual content like details/edit-in-place (use FlotoDrawer). Don't rely on the x or backdrop-click to close — both are disabled (F1), so always include a footer Cancel.
MModal.example: The metric-explorer Forecast / Anomaly / Compare / Arithmetic analysis modals, the Error modal, password-verify, chart capture, and linked-records detail dialogs.

FlotoConfirmModal.useWhen: Confirming a yes/no or destructive action before it runs. Drive the open prop (boolean); use icon + message slots, successText/cancelText, variant="error" for destructive; listen to @confirm / @hide. Cancel sits left, the action right.
FlotoConfirmModal.dontUse: Don't use for a focused task or form that needs body input (use MModal). Don't label the actions Yes/OK — name the verb (Delete, Save). For a brief success/error message, use a notification instead of a confirm modal.
FlotoConfirmModal.example: Delete confirmations across CRUD lists (paginated-crud), inline name edit, widgets, rediscover, domain-mapping, and trap-profile delete — Delete monitor? with error variant and Cancel/Delete.

restrict-width.useWhen: You need a fixed wide modal (side-by-side comparison, wide tables) at 1020px regardless of the width prop. Apply overlay-class-name="restrict-width" (forces content min = max = 1020px); often paired with scrollable-modal.
restrict-width.dontUse: Don't use for normal-width dialogs (use the width prop on MModal). Beyond a wide fixed modal, prefer a FlotoDrawer (the 85–96% full-screen pattern) rather than forcing 1020px.
restrict-width.example: The compare-metric and diff-view modals that show wide side-by-side content.

no-padding-modal.useWhen: The content manages its own padding — a code editor, a full-bleed list, or an embedded form — and the default modal padding gets in the way. Apply overlay-class-name="no-padding-modal" (body → 8px) or no-padding-confrim-modal (body → 0).
no-padding-modal.dontUse: Don't use for standard form/text dialogs that expect the default inset padding. This only strips padding; for scrolling long content combine with scrollable-modal, and for wide content with restrict-width.
no-padding-modal.example: The log-collection profile list, view-query, LAMA integration, and activation-code modals.

view-edit.useWhen: [element/composition] a detail modal that toggles a read-only VIEW and an EDIT form (the product is-view pattern) — show the record with obs-key-value + an Edit button; on Edit swap to obs-input `block` fields + a Cancel/Save footer.
view-edit.dontUse: for a big multi-section record → a drawer or full page; for a one-shot create form the edit form alone is enough.
view-edit.example: Edit monitor: view (Monitor/IP/Type/Polling) → Edit → the form → Save/Cancel back to view.

compare.useWhen: [element/composition] a side-by-side comparison — a restrict-width (1020px) modal holding two (or more) obs-key-value panels (e.g. two monitors' CPU/Memory/Disk/Status).
compare.dontUse: for a single record's detail (a normal-width detail modal) or many rows to compare (a table).
compare.example: Compare metrics: web-server-01 vs db-primary, colour-coded values + status tags.

inProduct.MModal: Anomaly/Forecast/Outlier modals, Filter modal, Note modal, Compare modal
inProduct.FlotoDrawer: detail/view drawers, form drawers (incident details, approval drawers)

do: Use MModal for a focused dialog; FlotoConfirmModal for confirms.
Always include a footer Cancel (visible way out).
Use FlotoDrawer for long or record-contextual content.
dont: Don't rely on a x or backdrop-click to close (disabled, F1).
Don't use a modal for content better inline or in a drawer.
Don't label actions Yes/OK — name the verb (Delete, Save).
whenToUse: A focused task, dialog, or confirmation that must interrupt the flow.
knownIssues: [element] obs-modal is FUNCTIONAL: a centered dialog on the native <dialog> (showModal) — top-layer, focus-trap, Esc, a blurred ::backdrop. `open` reflects to el.open (el.show()/el.hide() too). Variants: confirm (icon+message), hide-footer, no-padding, scrollable, restrict-width (1020px), width. The header always has a close ✕ (unlike the product's F1 note). Composes obs-button (footer) + obs-icon (✕/icon). For a full-screen flow use obs-drawer.

F1 (medium, UX/a11y): no top-right x and no backdrop-close (closable/maskClosable hardcoded false). Escape + footer Cancel work, but a modal whose footer omits Cancel has no discoverable dismiss for mouse users. Make closable a prop (visible x) or require a footer Cancel.
F2 (high, a11y): no visible focus ring inside the dialog (SF-001).

F3 (low): scrollable-modal sets a fixed-height flex-column body but NO overflow on the body — long content spills out unless wrapped in a flex:1;min-height:0;overflow-y:auto child. Add overflow to the variant or document the required structure.
changelog: 2026-08-09 — Slots + docs (consumer G6 follow-up): added a `footer` slot (custom modal footer, replacing the built-in Cancel/confirm buttons) and documented that `title` renders in BOTH the default header AND the confirm variant.

changelog.change: Completeness pass: declared the prop enums (variant: default/confirm; confirm-variant: primary/error), documented the default slot (body / confirm message) and the imperative show()/hide() API + the open pattern, and re-pointed the decision flow at the obs-* elements (obs-modal variant=confirm for confirms, obs-drawer for record-contextual/full-screen). Verified the playground reaches every variant (Detail · Confirm · Scrollable · Compare presets + hide-footer/no-padding/restrict-width/mask-closable toggles).

changelog: 2026-07-14: full docs + playground pass (owner) — the Details playground now exposes the WHOLE variant surface: a Scenario preset (Detail / Confirm / Scrollable / Compare — swaps the body + defining attrs) plus controls for title, variant, confirm-variant, confirm-text, cancel-text, width, hide-footer, no-padding, scrollable, restrict-width, mask-closable. Added the element 'variants & when to use' table + element props + composition usageRules (view-edit, compare) to the prose spec. Everything toggleable on one live modal.

2026-07-14: two missing example patterns added (owner) — (1) 'Edit record (view ↔ edit)': a detail modal that toggles a read-only VIEW (obs-key-value + an Edit button) and an EDIT form (obs-input fields + Cancel/Save), modelling the product's is-view record pattern. (2) 'Compare metrics': the restrict-width (1020px) modal now holds REAL side-by-side comparison content — two obs-key-value panels (web-server-01 vs db-primary) with color-coded values + status tags — instead of a placeholder. Both are composition examples (no new component API); they reuse obs-key-value / obs-input / obs-button.

2026-07-14: confirm variant matched to the product (owner) — the destructive confirm dialog was a vertical centered layout (icon on top, centered message + filled button); the real FlotoConfirmModal (.floto-confirm-modal) is HORIZONTAL: a coloured-border card (2px top/bottom, 4px left/right — red for error), an icon in a coloured-border CIRCLE on the LEFT, and the message + LEFT-aligned actions on the RIGHT with the confirm button OUTLINE (not filled). Rebuilt to match; the delete example now uses the product `trash` icon. Grounded in src/components/_base-confirm-modal.vue + src/design/modal.less.

2026-07-14: REAL fix — closed modals were visible/stacked in the gallery (owner). The `.modal` panel set `display:flex` UNCONDITIONALLY, and author CSS beats the UA `dialog:not([open]){display:none}` — so every CLOSED <dialog> rendered its content inline (visible + stacked), which is what made the Examples page look like all modals were open. Scoped the layout to `.modal[open] { display:flex }` so a closed dialog falls back to the UA display:none. (The earlier single-modal-invariant / no-auto-open changes were real but addressed a different symptom; this display bug was the actual cause. Lesson: verify overlay CLOSED state by computed `display`/visibility, not just the `.open` property.)

2026-07-14: single-modal invariant + no auto-open (owner) — the docs Examples page could stack/hang: a native <dialog>.showModal() allows only ONE modal in the top layer, so opening a second while one was open threw and fell back to an inline (backdrop-less) dialog that stacked. Fixed two ways: (1) opening any obs-modal now first closes whichever obs-modal is open (a module-level invariant across instances); (2) the docs playground no longer auto-opens on load — the modal renders CLOSED behind an 'Open modal' trigger (auto-opening blocked the page). Verified: 0 open on load, exactly 1 true top-layer modal at a time.

2026-07-13: shipped the real <obs-modal> web component — a centered dialog on the native <dialog> (showModal: top-layer, focus-trap, Esc, blurred ::backdrop). --primary title + close ✕, 24px body, Cancel + confirm footer; 16px corners (20px confirm). Variants: confirm (centered icon + message + Cancel/action), hide-footer, no-padding, scrollable, restrict-width (1020px), width. Reflects el.open; composes obs-button + obs-icon. Verified with match-component diff.mjs (specs/modal.mjs).

2026-06-07: added (decision-grade). MModal (39x) + FlotoConfirmModal (71x). Trigger-slot / open-prop; title/body/footer slots; width/centered/confirmLoading. Verified Basic + Confirm open; Escape closes, no x (F1). Drawer (158x) = related own entry.
$tokensNote: Backdrop scrim is a blurred Ant literal rgba(0,0,0,.45) + blur(3px) — not tokenized; Ant Modal internals follow the kit.

props.confirmLoading: Boolean — spinner on the confirm button
props.overlayClassName: String — class on the backdrop mask

FlotoConfirmModal.note: Confirm/alert wrapper — variant=error for destructive; commonly hosts a FlotoForm (form-in-modal).

a11y.summary: role=dialog; Ant traps + restores focus; Esc closes. No top-right × and no backdrop-close (closable/maskClosable hardcoded false). Give a clear title; state the consequence for confirms.
issues: No visible focus ring inside the dialog.
Esc is the only dismiss (no × / backdrop-close).
a11y.$note: Catalogue-wide gap SF-001 = no visible :focus-visible ring; tracked in findings/.

slots.footer: replaces the built-in Cancel/confirm footer buttons with your own actions (default variant).

methods.show: el.show() — open the modal (takes the top layer; closes any other open overlay).
methods.note: Or drive the `open` attribute. A modal must open on a user action (a trigger button), never auto-open on load.
